newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Man charged with six murders after NZ massacre.
newsitem.headline: Man charged with six murders after NZ massacre.

text.p: A man was charged with six counts of murder and eight counts of attempted murder in the Hamilton District Court on Wednesday in relation to Saturday's shotgun massacre that shocked New Zealand.

Stephen Anderson, of Wellington, was also charged with a firearm offence and remanded in custody until February 26 to the Tokanui Psychiatric Hospital, south of Hamilton, for a psychiatric assessment.
Dressed in white police overalls, Anderson, who is 24, not 22 as police had earlier said, stood upright and still in the dock and entered no plea.
The courtroom was packed with a heavy media contingent.
Defence lawyer Stuart Grieve QC said the state of Anderson's mind had already attracted intense media speculation, which was premature and "plainly sub judice".
Grieve asked the court that the press be reminded of its obligations, and Judge Geoffrey Rae said the media should ensure the law was obeyed in any pre-trial publicity.
Six people were killed and six wounded in a shotgun massacre in the small North Island settlement of Raurimu on Saturday.
Police took Anderson into custody about two and a half hours after the killings. He was found stark naked in farmland close to the murder scene.
Meanwhile, about 400 mourners attended a memorial service on Wednesday morning in the grounds of the former Raurimu school, a few hundred metres (yards) from the scene of the shooting.
Governor-General Sir Michael Hardie Boys and Prime Minister Jim Bolger also paid their respects and expressed their grief on behalf of the country.

Hardie Boys read out a message received from Queen Elizabeth and expressed hope that something positive would come out of the tragedy, while Bolger offered the sympathies of all New Zealanders, who he said had been devastated by Saturday's events.
"Out of this tragedy we not only reflect on the sadness but today it is also an occasion to reflect on the goodness of the lives that were lost," he said.
Reverend Val Riches reminded mourners of the beauty and tranquillity of Raurimu.

"The shooting tragedy on Saturday shattered its tranquillity and splattered its beauty with blood. Today we have gathered to reclaim this place for its people...to refuse anger, fear and blame and to support the families," she said.
"We stand here to say that this community will survive, this community will go on and continue to share its beauty and peace with all who come to visit this area."
As well as friends and families of those who died, local residents, police and other emergency service staff who helped after the tragedy joined the half-hour service.
Six residents of Raurimu later planted six totara trees and mourners sprinkled earth around them.
Saturday's slaying is the fifth mass slaughter in the 1990s that has shocked New Zealand and undermined its image as a safe and peaceful country.
